simple.meaning: שָׁלָה (shâlâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a wrong.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 3:29. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁלָה (H7955) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: שָׁלָה (shâlâh) / H7955 is traced through Daniel 3:29 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Therefore I make a decree, that every people, nation, and language, which speak anything evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill; because there is no other god who is able to deliver like this.”

definitions.full: H7955. shalah שָׁלוּ noun feminine neglect, remissness ( ᵑ7 id. ); — absolute ׳שׁ Ezra 4:22 ; 6:9 ; Dan 6:5 + 3:29 Qr; Kt שׁלה usually thought an error for שׁלו ; Hi Bev M (perhaps) explained as שֵׁלָה = שְׁאֵלָה = thing, affair ( 4:14 ).
